Send the prompts in llmention.yaml to each engine in each mode, then save the answers as a run and print the summary. Use --dry-run first. It sends nothing and shows how many requests the run would send and roughly what they cost, in total and for each engine. It also says which API keys are set. Ctrl+C stops the run and saves the answers that already came back. With --mock, the built-in mock engine makes up the answers for every engine, so you see the report for your own product without keys or cost. Those runs are saved apart from real runs, and `llmention report --mock` shows them.

Related commands:
  llmention report
  llmention init

Output:
  Shows text you can read in your terminal.
  Use --json to get JSON for scripts and other programs.
  Use --jq to filter the JSON output with a jq expression.
  Use --template to format the output with a Go template.

Usage:
  llmention run [flags]

Examples:
llmention run --dry-run
llmention run
llmention run --mock
llmention run --engine chatgpt --mode search
llmention run --fail-under mention-rate=40%
llmention run --suite recognition.basic
llmention run --json

Flags:
      --engine strings           Only ask these engines (ids from llmention.yaml, comma-separated)
      --fail-under stringArray   Fail with exit code 7 when a number is below a threshold, for example mention-rate=40% (repeatable)
  -h, --help                     help for run
      --judge                    Use the AI grader set up under analysis.judge
      --max-requests int         The most requests this run may send, retries included (default execution.max_requests)
      --mock                     Let the mock engine make up every answer, and save the run apart from real runs
      --mode strings             Only use these modes (no-search, search, forced-search, default)
      --repetitions int          Ask each prompt this many times (default from llmention.yaml)
      --suite strings            Run these suites instead of your prompts, for example recognition.basic

Global Flags:
      --config string     Path to the config file
      --dry-run           Preview changes without performing them
      --include-meta      Wrap the JSON output as {data, meta} with request details
      --jq string         Filter the JSON output with a jq expression
      --json              Output stable JSON instead of the human view
      --no-ansi           Disable all ANSI/control sequences in human output
      --no-color          Disable color in human output
      --no-pager          Never use a pager for long human output
      --no-prompt         Never block on an interactive prompt
      --quiet             Suppress non-essential output
      --template string   Format the JSON output with a Go text/template
